SYSTEMS.name: Power Contract Intelligence
SYSTEMS.line: Reads a tender pack and returns every risk and deviation cited to the page it came from.
SYSTEMS.lede: A pre-award workspace for power-sector supply and services bids. The tender pack goes in; risks, deviations, pre-bid queries and a clause map come out, and three review stages carry it to a go/no-go and a submission workbook.

gates.m: every position cited or counted as a gap

rule.long: A clause the extraction cannot verify against the source is counted as a gap, never as compliant. Citations resolve only to the passages the model was actually shown.

stops.d: Eleven document formats parsed per file, with a record of what parsed, what was empty, what failed and what was truncated.
Qualification and go/no-go, then bid strategy, then risk, compliance and submission, each answered by a reviewer.
Compliant, acceptable, deviation, silent, ambiguous or not assessed; silence is a finding.

stops.t: A workbook a committee can read
stops.d: Deviation register, bid risk register, pre-bid queries and pricing assumptions export as one workbook.

proof.d: Every pack is read against the same catalogue across six contract types, so coverage does not depend on who ran it.
Runs with on-device lexical retrieval and no model key; a language model is optional.

SYSTEMS.boundary: Runs entirely inside your perimeter with no API key. If a model is enabled, the provider and payload are named before deployment.

SYSTEMS.name: Sentinel
SYSTEMS.line: Turns a site photo into a cited countermeasure, and says so when the sources are too thin to answer.
SYSTEMS.lede: A mobile-first safety platform for plants and construction sites. A photograph becomes a classified hazard, a drafted report and a countermeasure cited to the safety literature; permits are audited from photos, and a risk assessment stops work when a high residual hazard remains.

rule.long: Below a grounding score of 30 out of 100, Sentinel returns the sources it found and does not generate an answer.

stops.d: A photo, or a safety clip sampled to five evenly spaced keyframes; the iOS app queues captures offline.
Dense and BM25 retrieval fused and reranked, with a grounding score, coverage and a citation chain.
Five permit types, five controls each; a permit passes, fails or is conditional.
Five activity templates; any hazard left at high residual risk forces a stop, recomputed on the server.

proof.d: Below it, Sentinel returns “insufficient sources” instead of an answer.
Thirteen hazard types and eight Lean waste types anchor classification and reporting.

SYSTEMS.boundary: The hosted reference runs in the Mumbai region; every create, update and delete is written to an audit log.

basis.corpus: api/data/chroma_safety: 2,833 chunks — OSHA 1,110, HSE 1,719, LEI 4 (no NFPA, NIOSH or OSH Code)

SYSTEMS.name: Labour Compliance
SYSTEMS.line: Closes the contract-labour month with every reminder and notice waiting for a person to approve it.
SYSTEMS.lede: Supervised month-close for principal employers of contract labour. Contractors upload their monthly records through a single-use link; registers and checklists are drafted, wages and contributions are reconciled against the officer’s portal attestation, and nothing is applied until a person approves it.

gates.m: single-use link per contractor and month

rule.long: The agents can only queue proposals. Nothing is applied, and nothing is recorded as sent, until a person approves it; a decided proposal cannot be decided again.

stops.d: A single-use link scoped to one contractor and one month; ECR, ESIC challan and wage register, and a phone photo is fine.
The central Acts and the four Labour Codes with the 2026 Central Rules; Code items are screening prompts.
Wages and contributions within ±2%, headcount exact; a mismatch is flagged for decision.
Approve or reject each proposal; approvals write to a hash-sealed evidence vault.

proof.d: Agents queue proposals; only a person’s decision applies one.
On wages and contributions against the attestation; headcount must match exactly.

reads: Four Labour Codes and Central Rules 2026
SYSTEMS.boundary: Contractor uploads are hashed and sealed on arrival; invite tokens are stored only as hashes.

basis.invite: lib/invites.ts:29-51; app/c/[token]/page.tsx; upload route 410 on expiry
basis.calendar: applicability.ts:56-57 (ECR/ESI day 15); Code obligations unscheduled, calendar.ts:84
basis.templates: lib/forms.ts:22-43 (9 templates, all DRAFT / NOT LEGALLY VALIDATED)
basis.approver: InboxClient.tsx:19 — approver identity is not authenticated yet

SYSTEMS.name: NexusRef
SYSTEMS.line: Connects project correspondence to its register, reference and revision.
SYSTEMS.lede: A project-correspondence workspace for incoming mail, letters and attachments. Configured routing and classification help put the record in the right project; formal references and revisions keep it identifiable, and uncertain classification is marked for review.

gates.m: project and folder IDs checked against the tenant

rule.long: Classification without a folder, or with confidence below 0.4, is marked for triage. That flag identifies uncertainty for review; it is not a blanket prohibition on automatic mailbox filing.

stops.d: Incoming correspondence is brought into a project register with the files that accompany it.
Configured routes, recognised senders and content help identify the project and folder. Model suggestions are checked against the available tenant records.

stops.t: A reference that carries its context
stops.d: Tenant, project, correspondence type, year and sequence form the reference; a version suffix distinguishes revisions.
Low-confidence classification is marked for triage so the team can review the filing context.

proof.d: A missing folder or classification confidence below 0.4 is marked for review.
Formal references carry the tenant, project, type, year, sequence and version.

SYSTEMS.boundary: Mailbox access, storage and optional model providers are agreed for the deployment. Automatic administrative filing follows the configured workflow; issued positions and outgoing correspondence remain with your team.

SYSTEMS.name: OneLegal
SYSTEMS.line: Runs a contract through a 301-question playbook, scores every clause for risk, and drafts notices and claims only from evidence counsel has sealed.
SYSTEMS.lede: A contract risk review and claims workbench for in-house counsel and commercial teams. The playbook leads: 301 questions across eleven contract families, each answer cited to its clause and each clause scored against a market baseline. When a dispute follows, counsel seals an evidence set, and notices and claims draft only from what is under the seal.

gates.m: each clause 1–5 against a market baseline

rule.long: Drafting refuses to run over an evidence set that has not been sealed, before any model is called. Once sealed, an edit is refused.

stops.d: EPC/FIDIC, IChemE, Orgalime, NTPC GCC and common commercial forms, 301 questions in all.
Hypothetical-answer, context-aware and keyword passes fuse dense and BM25 results before reranking.

stops.t: An evidence set counsel signs off
stops.d: A SHA-256 manifest freezes the evidence used for drafting.

stops.t: Notices and a Statement of Claim
stops.d: EOT, delay, cost and variation notices, and a Statement of Claim, drawn only from sealed evidence.

proof.d: Across eleven contract families, each scored against its own market baseline.
Filing, signing, serving, sending, deleting a record and confirming a deadline go to counsel by hand.

reads: EPC / FIDIC Silver and Yellow baseline
SYSTEMS.boundary: Model routing is per feature; which provider handles each feature is set with you and written down before deployment.

basis.routing: model_router.py:45,138-150 (defaults to xAI Grok; LM Studio optional)

pci.headline: See the risk before you bid.
pci.summary: Bring the tender pack into one review. Find the contractual risks, prepare deviations and pre-bid queries, and give the bid team a clearer basis for its decision.
pci.challenge: Conditions, schedules and appendices arrive as separate files. The difficult part is seeing which terms change the commercial position, what is missing and what needs a question before submission.

delivers.d: Risks and compliance positions linked to the source text, with silent and ambiguous terms identified.
A deviation register, bid risk register, pre-bid queries and pricing assumptions in one export.

delivers.t: A basis for the bid decision
delivers.d: Qualification, strategy and compliance reviews for the people deciding whether and how to bid.

pci.review: Your team determines qualification, accepts commercial exposure and approves the submission. A clause that cannot be verified is recorded as a gap.
pci.example: A tender clause cannot be verified against its source. It appears as a gap for review and a possible pre-bid query; it is not presented as compliant.

onelegal.audience: Counsel · contracts, commercial and claims teams
onelegal.headline: Know the risk. Build the claim.
onelegal.summary: Run the contract through a playbook of 301 questions. Every answer is cited to its clause and every clause is scored against a market baseline. When a claim follows, notices and a Statement of Claim draft from evidence counsel has sealed.
onelegal.challenge: Contractual risk is fixed when the contract is signed and tested when something goes wrong. The team needs to see which clauses carry the exposure before it signs, and a claim needs a clear link between what is asserted and the record relied upon.
onelegal.input: The contract set, and for claims a curated evidence set

delivers.d: 301 playbook questions across eleven contract families, each answer cited to its clause and each clause scored against a market baseline.
Counsel curates and seals the material that governed drafting may use.
EOT, delay, cost and variation notices, and a Statement of Claim, prepared from sealed evidence.

onelegal.review: Counsel selects the evidence and reviews the legal position. Filing, signing, serving and sending remain human actions; the system does not perform them.
onelegal.example: Drafting is requested before the evidence set is sealed. The request is refused before a model is called, so the draft cannot proceed on an unapproved record.

sentinel.audience: Site teams · EHS and permit reviewers
sentinel.headline: Make the observation actionable.
sentinel.summary: Turn a site photograph into a structured hazard report, retrieve cited countermeasures and review permit controls with the evidence in view.
sentinel.challenge: An observation is useful when it becomes a record someone can assess and act on. The photograph, hazard, advice and permit checks need to stay connected.
sentinel.input: Site photos, clips and permit evidence

delivers.d: Photo or clip evidence supports classification, report drafting and the observation record.
Retrieved safety literature is linked to the response, with a grounding score showing whether enough support was found.
Photo-based permit checks and point-of-work risk assessments support the responsible person’s review.

sentinel.review: The responsible person assesses the finding and decides the site response. Where source support is below the grounding floor, the system does not generate an answer.
sentinel.example: The retrieved material scores below 30/100. The system returns the sources it found and insufficient-source status, rather than generating advice.

labour-compliance.headline: Close the month with the record in view.
labour-compliance.summary: Collect contractor records, reconcile wages and contributions, and bring proposed reminders, notices and register updates to a person for approval.
labour-compliance.challenge: Monthly records arrive from different contractors in different formats. The employer needs to see missing submissions and reconciliation differences before deciding what follows.

delivers.d: Scoped upload links collect records for one contractor and one month, including phone photographs.
Wages, contributions and headcount are checked against the officer’s portal attestation; mismatches are flagged.
Reminders, notices and updates arrive as proposals. A person approves or rejects each before it is applied.

labour-compliance.review: Your officer reviews exceptions and approves proposed actions. Generated forms are drafts for review; they do not establish that statutory obligations have been discharged.
labour-compliance.example: A reconciliation difference is flagged and a proposal is queued. No change is applied until a person approves it.

nexusref.headline: Keep the project record connected.
nexusref.summary: Bring incoming correspondence into a project register. Route mail and attachments, assign formal references and keep revisions identifiable, with uncertain classification marked for review.
nexusref.challenge: Project mail arrives across inboxes, with attachments, repeated subjects and changing revisions. The team needs a connected record that can be found, referenced and reviewed in context.

delivers.d: Incoming mail and attachments are connected to their project and filing context.
References include the project, type, year and sequence, with a version suffix for revisions.
Missing folders and classification confidence below 0.4 are marked for triage.

nexusref.review: Routine administrative filing can run under configured rules. Your team reviews uncertain classification and remains responsible for issued positions and outgoing correspondence.
nexusref.example: A message has no clear folder and the classifier assigns confidence below 0.4. The classification is marked for triage so the team can resolve its filing context.

vision.title: A better tomorrow, built around people.
vision.statement: A future where technology makes complex work leaner, gives teams room to innovate, and helps them stand by decisions that create lasting impact.
vision.foot: Clarity to act. Confidence to decide. Room to innovate.

mission.title: Complex operations. Lean digital workflows.
mission.statement: We transform complex operations into lean digital workflows by removing friction, improving efficiency and making decisions easier to audit, explain and defend.
mission.method: Six moves from the Lean tradition, starting where the work is done.

MISSION.d: Start where the work is done, with the records it already produces.
Every step from input to sign-off, drawn as it actually runs.
The current best way, written down, then repeated by the system.
Activity that consumes time and adds no value is taken out.
A check that makes the wrong result impossible to pass downstream.
The system raises the problem and calls a person, and every decision is auditable from input to sign-off.

ABOUT.title: Technology shaped around people.
ABOUT.lede: We build intuitive digital workflows that give you the clarity to innovate, confidence to stand by your choices and tools to create lasting impact.
body: We start with the people doing the work: the tender that has to be priced by Friday, the correspondence a project has to keep connected, the contractor records that have to be reconciled. We map the process before building the technology and remove waste and rework.

We write down what each system does, what it refuses to do, and what is not built yet. If a claim on this site does not survive being checked against the code, we would rather correct it than keep it.

DEPLOYMENT.title: Where your data lives is your choice.
DEPLOYMENT.lede: Choose the operating boundary. We document every data path before go-live.

options.d: Inside your perimeter, governed by your identity, storage, backup and retention controls.
options.foot: Hardware you own · audit you control

options.d: Inside your tenancy. You retain the account, audit trail and control plane.
options.foot: Provider you approve · controls you retain

options.d: Scoped to an India region, with residency, subprocessors and access controls written into the agreement.

commitments.d: Customer material is not used to train product models.
Service and payload are identified in writing before deployment.
If nothing may leave your network, we scope it that way.

notBuilt.d: Our own hosting is an India region but not an empanelled offering. Deploying into your tenancy sidesteps this.

notBuilt.t: Encryption at rest, applied by the application
notBuilt.d: On your infrastructure, the disk and volume encryption you already run covers this. As a hosted service, it is work we still owe you.
Authentication and integration differ by product. Directory integration, access roles and the controls needed for your deployment must be verified in its scope.

notBuilt.t: A formal retention, deletion and legal-hold policy
notBuilt.d: Deployed with you, retention follows your policy on your storage. As a product feature, it is not there yet.

VALUES.d: We remove bloat, unnecessary complexity and administrative friction so teams can focus on work that matters. Lean means intentional, thoughtful craftsmanship.
Complex work needs a clear structure. We make the process, evidence and decision points easier to understand, so teams can act with confidence.
Efficiency should give people time and energy back. We build sustainable workflows that respect attention and support teams without making burnout the price of progress.
Every feature, architectural choice and process should add useful value for those who rely on it. We favour meaningful outcomes over more software.
